key_insight: Coupling teacher calibration with student learning can remove persistent teacher bias in LLM distillation and drive the student toward the oracle policy even without target-domain reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical distillation recipe for domain-shifted LLM deployment, enabling safer student models when target labels or rewards are unavailable.
method: Calibrate the teacher on source-domain reward feedback using token-level branching.
Use the calibrated teacher to train the student on target questions.
Feed the updated student back into later calibration rounds to reduce bias over iterations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical convergence guarantee: the student’s expected average KL divergence to the oracle student goes to zero at a polynomial rate.
watch_item: The guarantee relies on an autoregressive policy framework and source-domain reward feedback, so performance may depend on how well source calibration transfers under strong distribution shift.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
